story_retold_as_causal_chain: Tanana Chiefs Conference announced an AI note-taking tool, so consenting patients can have appointments recorded and draft notes prepared for provider review, but the notice supplies no measured benefit and leaves the retention period for de-identified portions unclear, which means patients have a real decision to make and can decline or change their minds with TCC's promise that their care will not be affected.

every_named_actor_as_established_by_scri.name: Tanana Chiefs Conference / TCC
every_named_actor_as_established_by_scri.established_identity: An Interior Alaska tribal health organization introducing Sully.ai; it states the recording policy and promises that declining will not affect care.

every_named_actor_as_established_by_scri.name: Sully.ai
every_named_actor_as_established_by_scri.established_identity: An AI paperwork tool that listens with patient permission and drafts appointment notes; it does not make medical decisions.

other_actor_roles: The patient gives permission, can decline, and can change their mind.
The provider reviews, edits, and approves a draft before it can enter the medical record.
An unnamed technology company may use de-identified portions of recordings to improve the system; its identity is not explicitly established.

single_question_answered.question: What changes when a patient says no to this AI note taker?
single_question_answered.answer: The patient can decline the recording or change their mind, and TCC promises their care will not be affected; the script explicitly says that promise has not been independently tested.
